data.description:
## Goal

Evaluate the effectiveness of Stage 1 (fast-mode contention queue depth 3→8 / wait 45s→120s) against the baseline: did local busy time and capture rise, and did the guardrails stay flat?

## Method

1. Wait until a comparable 24h window has elapsed post-change (same weekday mix where possible), then run the canonical analysis:
   `python3 .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --hours 24`
2. Compare against the 2026-10-14 baseline (archived at `/home/rgardler/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-14_2/`): busy 36.5%, local capture 14.5%, `fallback_after_queue` 1,871, p90 TTFT 16.4s total / 10.1s fast.
3. Metrics to report, split Total/Fast/Cheap where available:
   - Local busy time % and total compute (hours)
   - Local capture rate (local served / total demand)
   - `fallback_after_queue` and `local_lease_active` counts
   - p90 / median TTFT and Time-to-completion
   - Peak concurrency vs slot count (1 fast / 3 cheap)
   - Error tick: `slot_save failed`, `backend_retry`, upstream HTTP errors
   - Queue behaviour: contention-queue events and wait distribution from the proxy log

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Local capture rate (local served / total demand) is higher than the 14.5% baseline.
- [ ] All guardrail metrics are flat or improved; no critical regression.
- [ ] An explicit verdict per metric: improved / flat / regressed, each with the before/after number.
- [ ] An overall keep/revert recommendation with justification, recorded on this item.
- [ ] If the outcome is inconclusive (window too short, mixed traffic), state exactly what additional data is needed and when to re-run.
- [ ] Findings fed back to the parent epic LP-0MV8805WF007LTZA as a comment.

## Notes

- This is an analysis-only item: no proxy config changes here.
- The baseline `fast_sessions.csv` / `cheap_sessions.csv` are the comparison substrate; the report's Summary-by-hour table shows the temporal demand profile to control for weekday variation.
